correctness.rationale: For each \(m\ge3\) and \(t>0\), compactness and the Courant–Fischer variational representation ensure a symmetric optimizer; the exact star characteristic polynomial reduces its gap to one scalar z and a derivative sign (m-1)[(m+1-2z)^2-t z^2]. The single critical root produces precisely the two branches, and the global uniqueness argument independently rules out symmetry-breaking solutions using a simple gap eigenvector above the threshold and PSD contrast vectors at/below it. Zero-weight boundary is disconnected. The SymPy checker symbolically confirms all nontrivial simplifications and 58 rational checks, but the proof covers the infinite domain. No known logical gap remains after explicit boundary review.

originality.rationale: The novelty is the explicit sharp \(t=(m-1)^2\) threshold, closed-form optimizer and gap for all \(m\ge3\), and uniqueness under free individual rates. Sun–Boyd–Xiao–Diaconis (2006) formulate the exact general weighted-cost continuous-time FMMP SDP, so the general problem and its dual are prior art; the examined primary full text gives explicit paths and cycles, not the theorem. Ghosh–Boyd give concavity/symmetry, and Shakeri et al. address multiplex interlayer budgets, neither gives the specific branch/uniqueness statement. Results and aliases were compared in published-finding corpus and web searches, with explicit historical residual risk.
residual_risks: The general heterogeneous-cost FMMP semidefinite program (Sun et al., 2006) already contains this instance; novelty is claimed only for the exact all-star-size, one-priced-edge closed forms, phase threshold and uniqueness, not for optimization problem or framework.

Fiedler (1990, 1993) obtained tree absolute algebraic connectivity for equal costs; a less visible result specializing his or later dual arguments to the present unequal-cost star case may exist and warrants independent historical checking.

value.rationale: The instance is a canonical diffusion network whose sole expensive bridge cannot be removed. The theorem gives a complete rate-allocation law and a sharp, non-obvious threshold at a squared leaf-count price, including uniqueness despite eigenvalue multiplicity at the uniform optimum. It distinguishes when equal edge rates remain optimal in a heterogeneous budget and quantifies a lasting asymptotic gain (m+1)/m without requiring an SDP solve. General techniques are standard but this natural exact design rule and boundary are mathematically informative, not arbitrary finite enumeration.
